steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).

Stir oats, almonds, pecans, and sunflower seeds together in a large bowl. Mix oil, honey, cinnamon, and vanilla together in a smaller bowl; pour over dry ingredients and mix well. Spread mixture onto two ungreased baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden, about 20 minutes, stirring halfway through. Remove from the oven and let cool completely before storing.

raw_recipe.headline: Honey Nut Granola
raw_recipe.description: This easy honey nut granola recipe makes the most delicious granola! Mix together your favorite grains, seeds, and nuts, then bake until golden brown.
raw_recipe.name: Honey Nut Granola

review.reviewBody: Wow! I have made this granola 4 times since I found the recipe a few weeks ago. As soon as the family eats it up, I make more. I've changed it a bit each time, after reading all the reviews, and I think I've finally settled on my favorite: I use oats, sliced almonds and sunflower seeds (but no other nuts), whole flax seed, wheat germ (about 1/2 cup each)for added nutrition, plus coconut for sweetness. I up the oil and honey just a bit, plus add a bit of real maple syrup for flavor. I add a combo of regular and golden raisins, but only at the very end (otherwise they burn-yuck!). I bake it on parchment, on a lower temp (about 225) and stir often, every 7-10 minutes. I pulled it off to another pan to cool - trust me, this is a must! And then finally, since we like ours clumpy, as it was cooling, I pulled off bits and squeezed hunks together. I then mixed about half the still warm granola with about 1/3 cup powdered milk. It gave amazing flavor and texture to the finished product. This recipe is PHENOMENALLY good - and versatile and cheap. Wow, what's not to love?

With the cost of good granola going through the roof now I decided to start making my own. After looking at many recipes I picked this one and was not disappointed! I used the basic recipe but made my own additions/changes. I added about 3/4 c of ground flaxseed, used coconut oil in place of canola, added about 3 T. of maple syrup to oil/honey mix. I didn't have enough pecans so used what I had and added chopped walnuts to equal the 2 c nuts in recipe, as well as the rest of a bag of roasted/salted pumpkin seeds. Also added about 3/4 t. of salt to oil/honey/syrup mixture. I baked it a total of 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes. Perfect amount of time. Added dried chopped cherries to mix after taking out of oven. It's delicious!

This recipe is great! I used slivered almonds and substituted sunflower seeds. Because the slivered almonds are a fair amount larger and it looked a bit dry, I added a tablespoon of honey, which came out well. I used a big pan and a small pan and switched them after the second ten minute shift, then added ten more minutes. The big pan was on top first and I wouldn’t do it the other way around as the result was perfect.

Followed the recipe to the T but also incorporated some of the modifications to keep this as low calorie and healthy as possible - if that’s possible lol. Added flax seeds, coconut, did the 1/2 and 1/2 agave and honey mix, and added a conservative amount of big salt pieces. Doubled the amount of sweetener. Baked in a convection oven at 200 but had to for about 60 minutes stirring every 10-15 minutes. Also omitted any oil and just used some avocado oil spray (not too much). Granola came out very clumpy (woo hoo) and some parts were a bit sticky. I was nervous in the beginning as a lot of liquid was melted onto the parchment and I was hoping this didn’t turn into a watery granola but thankfully it didn’t. The chunks of pecans were also a GREAT addition because of the crunch. Would make again and try a higher temp. Curious to see if there’s a way to make it less sticky - but wondering if that’s why the oil is necessary?

This is amazing granola. My kids and husband eat it like cereal. The only thing I do differently is melt coconut oil instead of the canola oil, and did 1/2 honey and 1/2 pure maple syrup instead of ALL honey (to save on my honey). I cook it longer cause we like it extra crunchy. I love that there's no sugar in this. Guilt-free eating! It's fabulous on yogurt!

Good good good! Followed the recipe exact with the exception of cashews instead of pecans. After baking for 20 minutes, the mixture was a little too dry so I added another batch of wet ingredients. I was a little worried because it was very moist and wasn't sure it would dry enough to eat it but after another 15 minutes baking and cooled, it turned out great! Next time I may line my baking sheets with parchment paper as the mixture stuck pretty well to my cookie sheets...oh yeah I split the mixture into two batches as it made too much to fit on one sheet. I made one with cranberries and the other with chocolate chips

Super simple and easy recipe. Tip: if you like a looser granola, add a bit more oil and it will crumble apart very easily instead of in chunks. If you like it very chunky, maybe a bit less oil. I subbed the canola oil for olive oil because I never have canola on hand. I cooked at 275 and tossed every ten minutes. I think I ended up cooking it 35 minutes which made it perfectly golden brown. I think it took me so long because even though I cut the recipe in half, I probably could have still used two sheet pans. Also, I used honey and added some molasses because I’ve been on a molasses kick. Next time I’ll probably use more molasses. For seeds I only used roasted and salted pepitas and they turned out great. Nice and crunchy. Next time I’ll add flax seeds too. I added a pinch of salt as well. It’s a super easy recipe to make and nice to be able to customize and leave out a bunch of junk that would be in it at the grocery store.

I add ginger for a little bite. I also back off on the sunflower seeds and add milled flax seeds. I heat the honey mixture in the microwave so it spreads better. It’s made a HUGE difference. Even the kids like it!

My mom told me about this recipe. She doesn't add the sunflower seeds. I baked this at 7 minutes at a time, mixing in between, to total more than 20 minutes. I had it all on one pan and clumped it up a little at the end to make it more sticky. I added the Trader Joe's cran/blueberry/golden/raisin mix to it after it baked. I used this for teachers' gifts. It's also really yummy with dried strawberries!
I skipped the almonds (allergy) and put in puffed quinoa instead. Yum!

I love granola and this stuff is delicious! I am not eating processed sugar and the honey works perfectly adding a perfect amoung of sweetness. I added cashews instead of pecans and replaced the canola oil with coconut oil. I put the wet ingredients in a small pot on the stove first. I LOVE this stuff, SO delicious!
Quick, easy, and delicious. I didn't make any changes and it turned out perfect
Didn't have the various nuts provided so subbed in Nature's Source Salad Topping which has many of these nuts plus trail mix type indgredients.
Fantastic recipe! I have made this at least3 times now and each time it's better!!!
Super easy and delicious, you could of course add more honey if you prefer sweeter product or sprinkle with sugar when baking too. Will make again and again! Beats prepared product 100%
I used 2/3 cup of honey, + added 2 teaspoons Maple Extract. Plus after cooking, added 1 cup raisins, 1 cup dried cranberries, and about 15 dates, pitted and cut up. It was still just OK.

Easy is the first thing I look for in a recipe and this hit the spot. I used the nuts I like ( pecans and walnuts) and baked everything at 325. I will use this recipe instead of buying a 120z. bag of granola for $6.

I made this twice. I did a half recipe, used oats, pecans, walnuts, desiccated coconut, and added the raisins at the end, to prevent burning. As w other reviews, I stirred the mixture like 2x while baking. I baked for 30 minutes at 300 cause I like mine crunchy. I eat them w yogurt. Yummy!
This is my go-to recipe! Always enjoy it.
But bakes very quickly at elevation 6700. Burns easily. But we love it, we just have to watch it and tweek the time..
